subject: using loo() with ubms fitted model object

messages.author: f6c9ad244156b7ef
messages.subject: using loo() with ubms fitted model object
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have been fitting an occupancy model with package ubms, and am trying to deal with the various warning messages. At the moment, I keep getting a warning about some Pareto k diagnostic values being too high, and I am trying to get more information on the Pareto k values using the function loo(). However, loo does not seem to like ubmsFit objects, and it keeps throwing this error:

Error in UseMethod("loo") :
  no applicable method for 'loo' applied to an object of class "c('ubmsFitOccu', 'ubmsFit')"

Has anyone had this issue/found a way to work around it? I was running into this as well when I had divergent transitions and wanted to look at the pairs() plot, but it wasn't an issue because I was able to remove that warning by adding more iterations. 

I tried this with the crossbill dataset included in the ubms vignette as well, and it throws the same error for the loo() function. I'll note that in the vignette it did not throw warnings about pareto k diagnostic values (and shows that all pareto k values are good in the output of the loo() function for the global model), so I am unsure what is going on.

Thanks! I am entirely new to Stan, so any help would be much appreciated.

Best,

Rumaan

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: using loo() with ubms fitted model object
parts:
Hi Rumaan,

I can't replicate this problem, calling loo() on a ubms model returns output as expected in my tests. I wonder if in your R session you have also loaded another Stan-related package besides ubms, such as loo, rstan, etc. which is overwriting the ubms loo method. Maybe you could try running loo() on the model in an R session where the only package loaded is ubms (or perhaps load ubms last after all the others)?

If that doesn't work, if your model object is called "model", you can see the loo results by calling

model@loo

or

loo(model@stanfit)

This @stanfit slot in the model object contains the raw rstan output object, so you can call just about any other Stan-related function on that and get results.

Ken
